title: DISPATCH: Decreasing Intervention Using sFlt-1/PlGF Applied to Chronic Hypertension
official: Decreasing Intervention Using sFlt-1/PlGF Applied to Chronic Hypertension (DISPATCH Trial): A Pilot, Open-label, Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: This pilot study tests the feasibility of conducting an interventional study in pregnant people with chronic hypertension with interventional clinical management based on sFlt-1/PlGF. It will also collect data on time to delivery, the incidence of preterm delivery, and other maternal or neonatal complications, for a pivotal trial.

interventions.name: sFlt/PlGF lab assay with change in clinical care

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 and older
* Singleton living pregnancy
* Gestational age between 23+0 and 34+6 weeks gestation, confirmed by a fetal crown-rump length measurement in a first trimester ultrasound or by in vitro fertilization dates
* Chronic hypertension, defined as:

  * At least 2 blood pressure measurements 140 systolic or 90 diastolic 4 hours apart diagnosed at less than 20 weeks 0 days of gestation and within 12 months of conception.
  * History or current use of anti-hypertensive medications for the indication of lowering blood pressure within 12 months prior to conception or prior to 20 weeks 0 days in the current pregnancy. Use during a prior pregnancy and through 12 weeks postpartum, or use for stage 1 chronic hypertension are not exclusions.
* Evaluated in triage for worsening chronic hypertension, rule out preeclampsia due to:

  * Worsening blood pressures from baseline and/or development of severe range blood pressures
  * Preeclampsia associated symptoms: headache, vision changes, abdominal pain
  * New onset proteinuria or worsening proteinuria
  * Lab abnormalities suspicious for preeclampsia including anemia, signs of hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, increasing serum creatinine, elevated liver function tests
  * Any other concerning features of preeclampsia according to the evaluating clinician

Exclusion Criteria:

* Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelet syndrome (HELLP syndrome), pulmonary edema, eclamptic seizure, stroke, myocardial infarction, placental abruption, or heart failure.
* Absent or reversed end-diastolic flow in the umbilical artery Doppler
* Unable to consent
* Major birth defect or chromosomal abnormality that may necessitate preterm birth for other reasons
* Other pregnancy complication that may necessitate preterm birth (e.g., PPROM)
* IV Heparin use within 24 hours of the lab draw
* Exogenous PlGF-2 or PlGF-3 given for therapeutic use at a concentration higher than 100 pg/mL
